title: What numbers do these two Egyptian numerals stand for?
description: Two Egyptian numerals are read by the method of the solved example, adding the value of every symbol. The first has coils, heels and strokes, and the second has lotuses as well. Writing each number back in symbols checks the sums.
teaching_notes: One idea: add the value of every symbol, since each Egyptian symbol keeps its value wherever it sits. Read each numeral from the biggest landmark down. Watch for students who read the counts as digits.

video_script.why: The child uses the method of the solved example, adding the value of every symbol, on two new numerals.
video_script.substitution: Find the value of each kind of symbol, then add the values of all the symbols in the numeral.
video_script.anchor: two carvings, the first with 2 coils, 7 heels and 6 strokes, the second with 4 lotuses, 3 coils, 2 heels and 2 strokes
video_script.payoff_line: Add the value of every symbol in the numeral

final_answer.spoken: part one is two hundred seventy six, and part two is four thousand three hundred twenty two

never_show: the answer card before the last beat of the board solution
maths_rules: (i) 2 coils make 200, 7 heels make 70, 6 strokes make 6: 200 + 70 + 6 = 276
(ii) 4 lotuses make 4000, 3 coils make 300, 2 heels make 20, 2 strokes make 2: 4000 + 300 + 20 + 2 = 4322
check: 276 and 4322 written back in symbols give the same counts
video_script.design: One idea: add the value of every symbol. The two carvings stay on the stage and each kind of symbol lights up with its value.

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, read the second numeral.

<bookmark mark='m4'/>Two heels make twenty, and two strokes make two.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Four thousand plus three hundred plus twenty plus two makes four thousand three hundred twenty two.
